Truncate a post to its first five characters, where a character may be an emoji or any other Unicode.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/micro-blog) (MIT). Listed under [Strings & Text](/examples/?subject=strings-and-text).

```nomi-run
// FILE: micro_blog.nomi
//# Truncates a post to its first five characters.

/// The first five characters of `post`, or all of it when it is shorter. A
/// character is a grapheme, so an emoji is one, however many bytes it takes.
pub fn truncate(post: String) -> String {
    String.take(post, 5)
}

// FILE: micro_blog_test.nomi
import micro_blog

test "truncate" {
    cases = [
        #("English language short", "Hi", "Hi"),
        #("English language long", "Hello there", "Hello"),
        #("German language short (broth)", "brühe", "brühe"),
        #("German language long (bear carpet → beards)", "Bärteppich", "Bärte"),
        #("Bulgarian language short (good)", "Добър", "Добър"),
        #("Greek language short (health)", "υγειά", "υγειά"),
        #("Maths short", "a=πr²", "a=πr²"),
        #("Maths long", "∅⊊ℕ⊊ℤ⊊ℚ⊊ℝ⊊ℂ", "∅⊊ℕ⊊ℤ"),
        #("English and emoji short", "Fly 🛫", "Fly 🛫"),
        #("Emoji short", "💇", "💇"),
        #("Emoji long", "❄🌡🤧🤒🏥🕰😀", "❄🌡🤧🤒🏥"),
        #("Royal Flush?", "🃎🂸🃅🃋🃍🃁🃊", "🃎🂸🃅🃋🃍"),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, post, expected), description {
        assert micro_blog.truncate(post) == expected
    }
}

// Not a canonical case: the canonical data avoids characters made of several
// codepoints. A family emoji is five codepoints joined into one grapheme, and
// an "e" with a combining accent is two, so each counts as one character.
test "graphemes of several codepoints" {
    assert micro_blog.truncate("👨‍👩‍👧 ok and more") == "👨‍👩‍👧 ok "
    assert micro_blog.truncate("cafés") == "cafés"
}
```

## How it's written

- `truncate` is `String.take(post, 5)`. A `String` is iterated, counted and taken by grapheme cluster, so an emoji is one character, and so is a letter with a combining accent. The exercise's trap, counting UTF-16 code units or bytes, has no API to fall into.
- The canonical data avoids characters of more than one codepoint. A test marked as not canonical adds two: a family emoji (five codepoints joined by zero-width joiners) and an `e` followed by a combining acute accent. Both count as one character, where a codepoint count would cut them apart.
- The twelve canonical cases are one `subtests` table.
